Package com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.submission

Class OrderSubmissionService

java.lang.Object
com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.submission.OrderSubmissionService
@Service public class OrderSubmissionService extends Object
Service to orchestrate the order submission and execution lifecycle. Lifecycle: SUBMITTED -> ACCEPTED or REJECTED -> FILLED. All orders and executions are persisted for audit retention.

Order types: a MARKET order executes at once. LIMIT, STOP and STOP_LIMIT orders that can't fill yet are stored OPEN, holding back the cash or shares they may need (see ReservationService), and OrderTriggerEngine fills them through fillOpenOrder(java.util.UUID, java.math.BigDecimal, boolean, java.lang.String) once the market reaches their price.

Market hours (SessionPolicy): orders only execute in a session they may trade in - an order that would fill at once outside it is left OPEN instead, until that session comes. A market order placed outside regular hours is queued for the next open: it holds cash at its collar (ReservationService.collarFor(com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.order.Order.Side, java.math.BigDecimal)) and fills at the opening price, unless that is beyond the collar.

  • Method Details

    • submitOrder

      public OrderSubmissionResponse submitOrder(OrderSubmissionRequest request)
      Submits an order and, unless it has to wait for its price, executes it immediately.

      Runs in three steps rather than one transaction, because settling is account-app's work and it can only see what this app has committed (see FillRecorder): the order and its execution are committed first, then settled, and only then marked FILLED.

      If account-app doesn't answer settling with a refusal (it is unreachable, times out or fails), or the fill can't be recorded after settling, the order is returned ACCEPTED rather than failed: the trade may already have moved cash and holdings, and PendingFillRecovery finishes it.

      Parameters:
      request - the order submission request
      Returns:
      OrderSubmissionResponse containing order, execution, and balance details; an OPEN order has no execution yet
      Throws:
      org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException - not found (404) or forbidden (403) as account-app answers for the account, bad request (400) for any other account-app refusal, and service unavailable (503) if account-app can't be reached or fails during validation - before anything is stored

    • fillOpenOrder

      public Order.Status fillOpenOrder(UUID orderId, BigDecimal fillPrice, boolean stopReached, String bearerToken)
      Fills an OPEN order the market has reached the price of, as OrderTriggerEngine found. The order is checked again under its row lock - a cancel may have won - and the account is validated again, since cash or shares may have gone while it waited. Settling then follows the same steps as submitOrder(com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.submission.OrderSubmissionRequest).
      Parameters:
      orderId - the OPEN order to fill
      fillPrice - the price to fill at, the side's live executable price
      stopReached - whether this price reached the order's stop
      bearerToken - a settlement token issued to the order's owner, for account-app
      Returns:
      the order's status afterwards, or null if it was no longer OPEN
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if account-app can't be reached for validation; the order is left OPEN and tried again

    • expiryOf

      public static OffsetDateTime expiryOf(Order.TimeInForce timeInForce, OffsetDateTime now)
      When an order with the given time in force expires if it hasn't filled, with market hours off. With market hours on, see SessionPolicy.expiryOf(com.leap.leaplaughlove.order.order.Order.TimeInForce, java.time.OffsetDateTime, boolean, com.leap.leaplaughlove.common.market.MarketClock).
      Parameters:
      timeInForce - DAY or GTC
      now - when the order is placed
      Returns:
      midnight US Eastern time after placing for DAY, 90 days later for GTC
